02:42 -!- filip [Filip@193.190.11.245] has joined #linux4be
04:30 -!- MouseLRN [~mouse@caltrop.alt.iph.ras.ru] has joined #linux4BE
04:34 < filip> morning mouse
04:37 < MouseLRN> filip: good day ;-)
04:37 < filip> sdlregstat is really cool , just a couple of small issues (and it used the 'parachute'  a couple of times)
04:39 < MouseLRN> I know ;-)
04:41 < filip> I'm pretty sure there must be a register indicating if the value for x/y  is valid (reliable) or not. seen such a thing before with analog/digital convertors
04:42 < filip> so basically just add acheck to see if you should use the value or just ignore it. 
04:43 < filip> I've seen several controllers that contain double ADCcircuits, performing two conversions  and compare both results to see if they are close enough to be reliable
04:43 < MouseLRN> see source of regstat.c (kernel driver) and check line, where I return 0
04:45 < filip> is that test also in the sdlregstat I've been using ?
04:46 < filip> I get a  couple of noise samples at each pen up/down 
04:47 < MouseLRN> ?
04:52 < filip> as long as I keep stylus down, I  get no 'noise' and all seems perfect (but no calibaration so it is a little 'shifted')
04:53 < filip> but each time I do pen up/down, I get 2-4 'noise' pixels which are not accurate  (but relatively close, within 20 pixels  or so of the exact location)
04:59 < MouseLRN> I try to control it by cntrl register, but after touching some times, cntrl reg will always have 3704 instead 1304 (pen up). How to set reset to 1304 - I don't know (I can complete reset every time after touch, but it's incorrect) and need to disasm touch.dll
04:59 < filip> I see ...

The Vr41XX touch panel handler is complex; it handles filtering of noisy input data, and it generates mouse release events by using a timer
05:27 < MouseLRN> one moment
05:28 < filip> and http://www.ltc.com/linux-mips/tpanel.html : 
05:28 < filip> Bit 15 = xyz data valid, 1 is valid, 0 is invalid 
05:28 < filip> Bit 14 = pen contact state, 1 is down, 0 is up 
05:29 < MouseLRN> about linux-mips - this values produced by the tpanel driver, not hw
05:36 < MouseLRN> hmm, about Qt - I can rewrite driver, that will produce data in that structure... but I may have some trouble. I need to think.

05:56 < filip> could be worth a try  ?

06:00 < MouseLRN> I'll try it later
